cluster_summary: Across these reasons, the core pattern is that the scenarios are framed as zero-sum competitions, but the model overlooks the explicitly competitive motive in favor of a more generic self-conscious emotion. In both cases, the narrative clearly signals that the protagonist stands to gain if the rival is harmed—Ella’s envy of James’s painting and Claire’s advantage over Amy—yet the model gravitates toward guilt, fear, or reputational concern that the text never actually mentions. This suggests an overreliance on stereotyped moral-psychology heuristics and underweighting of concrete, situation-specific cues.
